231: This page features a single inspirational quote in large text: 'All individuals have become what they are because of their DOMINATING THOUGHTS AND DESIRES.' This quote serves as a thematic divider between Chapter 12 (The Brain) and Chapter 13 (The Sixth Sense), encapsulating a core principle: that one's dominating thoughts and desires shape one's entire identity and circumstances. The page bears the OceanofPDF.com watermark.
232: This page opens Chapter 13: THE SIXTH SENSE—The Door to the Temple of Wisdom (The Thirteenth Step to Riches). Hill states the Sixth Sense is the apex of The Think and Grow Rich Philosophy, through which Infinite Intelligence may and will communicate voluntarily, without any effort from or demands by the individual. It can be assimilated, understood, and applied ONLY by first mastering the other 12 principles. The Sixth Sense is that portion of the subconscious mind referred to as Creative Imagination—the 'receiving set' through which ideas, plans, and thoughts flash into the mind as hunches or inspirations. It defies description—cannot be described to someone who has not mastered the other principles because such a person has no knowledge or experience for comparison. Understanding comes only by meditation through mind development from within. The Sixth Sense is likely the medium of contact between the finite human mind and Infinite Intelligence, a mixture of both mental and spiritual. It is believed to be the point at which the human mind contacts the Universal Mind. After mastering all the success principles, one will be prepared to accept as truth a statement which may otherwise be incredible.
233: Hill makes the stupendous claim: Through the aid of the Sixth Sense, you will be warned of impending dangers in time to avoid them and notified of opportunities in time to embrace them. With development of the Sixth Sense, a 'Guardian Angel' comes to your aid, opening at all times the door to the Temple of Wisdom. Whether this is truth you will never know except by following the book's instructions. Hill states he is not a believer in nor advocate of miracles, because Nature never deviates from her established laws—some are so incomprehensible they appear as miracles. The Sixth Sense comes as near to being a miracle as anything he has experienced. He knows there is a power, or First Cause, or Intelligence which permeates every atom and embraces every unit of energy, and this Infinite Intelligence converts acorns into oak trees, causes water to flow downhill, follows night with day and winter with summer. This Intelligence may, through the principles of this philosophy, be induced to aid in transmuting DESIRES into concrete or material form. He has this knowledge because he has experimented with it and EXPERIENCED IT. Step by step through preceding chapters, readers have been led to this final principle. Those who have mastered each principle are prepared to accept the claims without skepticism.
234: Hill shares his personal experience with the Sixth Sense. During the age of hero worship, he found himself trying to imitate those he most admired, discovering that the element of FAITH gave him great capacity to do so successfully. He never entirely divested himself of this habit. His experience taught him that the next best thing to being truly great is to emulate the great by feeling and action. Long before writing for publication or delivering speeches, he followed the habit of reshaping his character by trying to imitate nine individuals whose lives had been most impressive: Ralph Waldo Emerson, Thomas Paine, Thomas A. Edison, Charles Darwin, Abraham Lincoln, Luther Burbank, Napoleon Bonaparte, Henry Ford, and Andrew Carnegie. Every night over a long period of years, he held an imaginary Council meeting with this group, whom he called his Invisible Counselors. Just before going to sleep, he would shut his eyes and see in his imagination this group seated with him around his Council Table, where he not only sat among those he considered great but actually dominated the group as chairman. His DEFINITE PURPOSE was to rebuild his own character to represent a composite of his imaginary counselors' characters. Realizing he had to overcome the handicap of being born into ignorance and superstition, he deliberately assigned himself voluntary rebirth through this method. Under 'Building Character through Autosuggestion,' he notes that all individuals become what they are because of DOMINATING THOUGHTS AND DESIRES, and self-suggestion is the sole principle through which character is built.
235: Hill describes his imaginary Council meetings in detail. He called on each Cabinet member for the knowledge he wished them to contribute, addressing each in audible words. To Emerson: he desired the marvelous understanding of Nature. To Burbank: the knowledge to harmonize Nature's laws, make cactus shed thorns, and make two blades of grass grow where one grew before. To Napoleon: the marvelous ability to inspire men and arouse them to determined action, and the spirit of enduring FAITH that turned defeat into victory—'Emperor of Fate, King of Chance, Man of Destiny, I salute you!' To Paine: freedom of thought and courage to express convictions. To Darwin: marvelous patience and ability to study cause and effect without bias or prejudice. To Lincoln: the keen sense of justice, untiring patience, sense of humor, human understanding, and tolerance. To Carnegie: a thorough understanding of the principles of organized effort used in building a great industrial enterprise. His method of addressing members varied according to the traits he was most interested in acquiring. He studied their lives with painstaking care. After some months, he was astounded to discover that these imaginary figures became apparently real—each developing individual characteristics that surprised him.
236: Hill continues addressing his Invisible Counselors. To Ford: he wished to acquire the spirit of persistence, determination, poise, and self-confidence which enabled Ford to master poverty and organize, unify, and simplify human effort. To Edison: he wished to acquire the marvelous spirit of FAITH with which Edison uncovered Nature's secrets, and the spirit of unremitting toil with which he wrested victory from defeat. After some months of nightly procedure, the imaginary figures became apparently real. Lincoln developed the habit of always being late, then walking around in solemn parade with hands clasped behind him, occasionally resting his hand on Hill's shoulder. He always wore an expression of seriousness—rarely smiling—the cares of a sundered nation making him grave. Burbank and Paine often indulged in witty repartee. One night Paine suggested Hill prepare a lecture on 'The Age of Reason' and deliver it from a church pulpit. Many laughed, but Napoleon groaned loudly—to him the church was but a pawn of the state. On one occasion Burbank was late, explaining he was experimenting with growing apples on any sort of tree. Paine chided him, reminding him it was an apple that started trouble between man and woman.
237: Hill continues the Council meeting anecdotes. Darwin chuckled, suggesting Paine should watch out for little serpents when gathering apples, as they had the habit of growing into big snakes. Emerson observed, 'No serpents, no apples,' and Napoleon remarked, 'No apples, no state!' Lincoln developed the habit of always being last to leave. On one occasion, he leaned across the table with folded arms, remained for many minutes, then lifted his head, walked to the door, turned back, laid his hand on Hill's shoulder and said, 'My boy, you will need much courage if you remain steadfast in carrying out your purpose in life. But remember, when difficulties overtake you, the common people have common sense. Adversity will develop it.' One evening Edison arrived early and said, 'You are destined to witness the discovery of the secret of life. When the time comes, you will observe that life consists of great swarms of energy, or entities, each as intelligent as human beings think themselves to be. These units of life group together like hives of bees and remain together until they disintegrate through lack of harmony.' Edison said these meetings would bring to Hill's rescue some of the same units of life which served the Cabinet members—units that are eternal and NEVER DIE. Edison was still living when this happened; Hill visited him and told him about the experience. Edison smiled broadly and said, 'Your dream was more a reality than you may imagine.' The meetings became so realistic that Hill became fearful and discontinued them for several months.
238: Hill recounts that some six months after discontinuing the practice, he was awakened one night—or thought he was—when he saw Lincoln standing at his bedside. Lincoln said, 'The world will soon need your services. It is about to undergo a period of chaos which will cause men and women to lose faith and become panic-stricken. Go ahead with your work and complete your philosophy. That is your mission in life. If you neglect it for any cause whatsoever, you will be reduced to a primal state and be compelled to retrace the cycles through which you have passed during thousands of years.' The following morning, Hill was unable to tell whether he had dreamed this or had actually been awake, but the experience was so vivid that he resumed his meetings the following night. At the next meeting, all members filed in together and stood at their accustomed places while Lincoln raised a glass and said, 'Gentlemen, let us drink a toast to a friend who has returned to the fold.' Hill began adding new members until the Cabinet grew to more than 50, including Christ, St. Paul, Galileo, Copernicus, Aristotle, Plato, Socrates, Homer, Voltaire, Spinoza, Kant, Schopenhauer, Newton, Confucius, Elbert Hubbard, Woodrow Wilson, and William James. This is the first time he had the courage to mention this in writing. He still regards the meetings as purely imaginary, but they led him into glorious paths of adventure, rekindled appreciation of true greatness, encouraged creative endeavor, and emboldened honest expression.
239: Hill states that somewhere in the cell structure of the human brain is an area which receives vibrations of thought called hunches. Science has not discovered where the Sixth Sense is located, but the fact remains that human beings do receive accurate knowledge through sources other than the five physical senses. Such knowledge is generally received when the mind is under extraordinary stimulation. Any emergency arousing the emotions and causing the heart to beat faster may bring the Sixth Sense into action—anyone who has experienced a near accident while driving knows the Sixth Sense often comes to the rescue by split seconds. During his meetings with the Invisible Counselors, Hill found his mind most receptive to ideas, thoughts, and knowledge reaching him through the Sixth Sense. He credits the Invisible Counselors entirely for ideas, facts, or knowledge received through inspiration. On scores of occasions when facing emergencies so grave his life was in jeopardy, he was miraculously guided past difficulties through the influence of his Invisible Counselors. His original purpose was solely to impress his subconscious mind through autosuggestion with certain characteristics he desired to acquire. In more recent years, his experimentation took a different trend—he now goes to his imaginary counselors with every difficult problem. The results are often astonishing, though he does not depend entirely on this form of counsel. The Sixth Sense will be of great interest and benefit to those whose aim is to accumulate vast wealth or accomplish great achievement, but need not claim the attention of those with more modest desires. Henry Ford undoubtedly understood and made practical use of the Sixth Sense. Thomas Edison understood and used it in connection with inventions.
240: Hill states that nearly all great leaders—Napoleon, Bismarck, Joan of Arc, Christ, Buddha, Confucius, and Mohammed—understood and made use of the Sixth Sense almost continuously. The major portion of their greatness consisted of their knowledge of this principle. The Sixth Sense is not something one can take off and put on at will. Ability to use this great power comes slowly, through application of the other principles. Seldom does any individual come into workable knowledge of the Sixth Sense before age 40. More often, the knowledge is not available until well past 50, because the spiritual forces with which the Sixth Sense is closely related do not mature and become usable except through years of meditation, self-examination, and serious thought. No matter who you are or your purpose in reading this book, you can profit by it without understanding this chapter—especially if your major purpose is accumulation of money or material things. This chapter was included because the book is designed to present a complete philosophy by which individuals may unerringly guide themselves in attaining whatever they ask of life. The starting point of all achievement is DESIRE. The finishing point is that brand of KNOWLEDGE which leads to understanding—understanding of self, understanding of others, understanding of the laws of Nature, and understanding and recognition of HAPPINESS. This sort of understanding comes in its fullness only through familiarity with and use of the Sixth Sense, hence the principle had to be included for those who demand more than money. Having read this chapter, one must have observed being lifted to a high level of mental stimulation. Hill advises returning to this chapter a month later, reading it again, and observing the mind soaring to a still higher level.
